The Future with Will, Going to, the Present Continuous and the Simple Present Tenses
You can use four different tenses to talk about the future.
When you talk about things that are not decided or when you make a decision at the moment of speaking for the future, you use the modal will.
When you ask about intentions, you use be going to.
When you talk about things that are arranged, on the agenda or booked for the future, you use the Present Continuous tense.
When you talk about schedules, you use the Simple Present.

You use reported speech when you are saying (reporting)  what other people said.
When you tell people what someone has said in the past, you generally make the verb tense 'more in the past'. You need to change the verb to the next past form.

You have to change the pronoun if you are reporting what someone else said. Compare these two sentences. In each case the person actually said "I don't want to go."

I said, “I don't want to go.” > I said I didn't want to go.
Bill said, “I don't want to go.” > Bill said he didn't want to go.
When you want to report questions asked, the subject normally comes before the verb.
Direct: Mr. Mitchell asks, “What is your experience in digital marketing?”
Indirect: Mr. Mitchell asked what your experience in digital advertising was.
When the question is a yes/no questions, you use if or whether to report it.
They asked if you had experience in sales.
Our COO said he was impressed by your skills, professional background and qualifications.

Kristi: Hey, Adam. Did you get any news from the publishing company?
Adam: Yes, I just got this letter. I hope I get the job! If not, I will have bought this tie for nothing!
Kristi: What does it say?
Adam: I'm going to read it right now.

Dear Mr. Bari,

As you know, the human resources department at Never Odd Or Even received many applications for the position of Web Content Editor. We regret to inform you that the selection committee has decided to offer the position to another candidate.

You made a strong impression during your phone interview and at the on-site interview. Our COO said he was impressed by your skills, professional background and qualifications.

Although we cannot offer you employment at this time, other employment opportunities may arise in the future, particularly in sales. The publisher Mr. Mitchell asked what your experience in digital advertising was. If you have any sales experience, could you please update your résumé and send it back to us? We will keep it on file in the case that a suitable position arises.

Kind regards,

Julia Allen
Manager of Human Resources

Kristi: You didn't get the job, but it's not all bad! It's great they asked if you had experience in sales.
Adam: You're right. I'm sending a short note back to them in a moment.
Kristi: That's a good idea.
Adam: I'm going to continue looking for work in the same field, so I think it's important to maintain good relationships. I have a meeting with a recruiter next week.

Dear Ms. Allen,

Thank you for your letter as a follow up from my interview at Never Odd Or Even. I truly appreciate the opportunity to meet your team. I do not have any experience in digital marketing or sales at the present time, but I'll be exploring possibilities in that area in the future.

Sincerely,

Adam Bari
